patch.value:
## Measured 2026-07-31 at HEAD across nineteen read surfaces

The published extraction contract is `.row_contract.jq_selector`, whose value on every surface that emits it is:

```
.row_contract.row_keys[] as $key | .[$key][]?
```

That expression is a pure function of `row_keys`. When `row_keys` is empty or absent, it yields nothing — always, regardless of what the envelope actually contains.

| class | surfaces | count |
|---|---|---|
| contract usable (`row_keys` populated) | list, search, history, activity, health, next, context | 7 |
| contract present but vacuous (`row_keys: []` or absent, selector still published) | deps, stats, aggregate, get | 4 |
| no `row_contract` at all | comments, notes, files, docs, graph, contracts, validate | 7 |
| no envelope (NDJSON stream, no contract possible) | events | 1 |

## The defect this item owns

The middle class. `pm deps pm-doxj --json` emits:

```
"row_contract": {"command":"deps","row_keys":[],"fields":"unsupported",
                 "jq_selector":".row_contract.row_keys[] as $key | .[$key][]?"}
```

The item has 18 dependency edges. The published selector returns zero rows. `pm stats --json` behaves identically while carrying `by_type` and `by_status` collections.

A missing contract fails loudly: the agent sees `null`, knows the surface is not covered, and special-cases it. A vacuous contract fails silently: the agent runs the documented one-liner, gets an empty stream, and cannot distinguish "this surface never populates row_keys" from "the query matched nothing". Silence is the worse failure because it is indistinguishable from a legitimate empty result, and every downstream count, loop and guard reads zero.

## Relationship to the general row-contract programme

`pm-sb0tns` owns the general problem — that no single shell or jq expression works across pm — and its acceptance criteria already require a documented one-liner exercised by a test, and require surfaces that cannot project fields to state why. This item is the narrow, immediately fixable subset: a surface that declares `fields: "unsupported"` and carries no row keys must not also publish a selector that is guaranteed to return nothing. Either it names its real row collection, or it omits `jq_selector` so the absence is visible.

This is not a request to make every surface projectable. It is a request that the self-describing contract never describe itself falsely.

## Minimal correct shape

- A surface that has row collections populates `row_keys` with their real key names, even when `--fields` is unsupported. `deps` has `nodes` and `edges`; `stats` has its count maps; `aggregate` has its groups.
- A surface with genuinely no row collection omits `jq_selector` entirely, or sets it to a value the contract defines as "no rows on this surface".
- A gate asserts the invariant directly: for every read command, if `row_contract.jq_selector` is present then evaluating it against the same envelope must return the same row count the envelope actually contains. That is checkable without knowing anything about the individual command.
Four read surfaces publish a jq_selector that is guaranteed to return nothing: the self-describing row contract is present, vacuous, and indistinguishable from an empty result
deps, stats, aggregate and get emit the universal jq_selector with row_keys empty, so the documented extraction one-liner silently yields zero rows on surfaces that demonstrably have rows.

No read surface publishes a jq_selector that cannot return the rows its envelope contains; Surfaces with row collections populate row_keys with the real key names even when --fields is unsupported; A gate evaluates each read command envelope against its own published selector and asserts the returned row count matches the envelope contents; Surfaces that emit no envelope at all (the NDJSON event stream) are declared as such in the contract documentation rather than discovered by a parser returning null
Makes the one published extraction expression trustworthy, which is the precondition for every shell and jq workflow the product advertises.
The composability principle promises grep/jq pipelines; a contract that lies by returning empty is worse for a scripted agent than no contract at all.
If a read surface publishes jq_selector, evaluating it returns the rows the envelope contains.
deps (18 edges), stats, aggregate and get publish the selector with row_keys empty; it returns zero rows on all four.
